title: Crack across the plate
blurb: Lincoln's glass negative cracked in 1865. The break crosses hair and background, which the surroundings constrain.
credit: Alexander Gardner, Feb 5, 1865 (print at the National Portrait Gallery, photographed by PatDavid). Wikimedia Commons

title: Faces that could have been (simulated)
blurb: Simulated damage: we tore a hole through Lincoln's eye on a public-domain photo, so the true face is known. Every restored eye here is invented, and the seeds disagree.
credit: Alexander Gardner, Feb 5, 1865 (print at the National Portrait Gallery, photographed by PatDavid). Wikimedia Commons. Hole added by the Cold Case team as a simulated test.

title: Barely damaged
blurb: Only the top-left corner of the glass plate is broken. Almost every pixel is original.
credit: Visconde de Vale Paraíso, Tennis group, Funchal, c. 1905. Arquipélagos / Wikimedia Commons

title: Crack network
blurb: Scratches run across the face and the background.
credit: Portrait of a man, Fonds Trutat, Bibliothèque de Toulouse. Wikimedia Commons
license: No known copyright restrictions (Bibliothèque de Toulouse, Flickr Commons)

title: Faces lost to damage
blurb: Heavy emulsion loss across a group portrait. Much of what's restored on these faces has to be invented.
credit: Group portrait including Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson, photographer unknown. National Library of Norway / Wikimedia Commons
